current.text: He has a hamstring injury and misses the preseason. He is to be re-evaluated in week one and might miss one or two games, or none.
Charlotte traded away LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, which opens usage on the team.
His usage should rise from 22% to about 24 or 25%, with about 32 minutes. He should take more shots and also commit more turnovers.
He is expected to take on more of the creation load, ahead of Brandon Miller, and his assists may rise. Walker calls him a good passer.
Experts expect his shooting efficiency to drop without LaMelo Ball setting him up. Several say the gain in usage and assists may be offset by worse efficiency.
Experts agree he is overpriced at a market rank in the 30s and 40s. His right range is the 60s. Do not take him in the top 50 or in rounds 3 or 4. One speaker would take him at a rank around 90.
In an expert mock auction he sold for 13 USD.
Josh would not pay more than 8 USD for him in an auction.
Projected starters are White, Knueppel, Miller, Reid and Diabaté. Grayson Allen starts while Knueppel is out.
Coby White is out with a calf injury and will probably miss the start of the season. Ball handling is to be split among White, Knueppel and Miller, with no single lead creator.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes.
Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, and has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte's two-game week starting March 1 should not factor into decisions about him.

durable.text: Threes are his standout category. He made 3.4 threes a game on 42% from three, and his projected volume is far above the top 250 pool.
He does little beyond points and threes. He gets few steals and blocks and is not a big rebounder.
His shooting was strong overall, 48% from the field, but not in games he played without LaMelo Ball.
As a rookie he finished 66th in category leagues but fell to 91st over the final two months, a partial rookie wall.
His game is not friendly to points leagues. He ranked 66th in 9-cat and 89th in points leagues last season.

note: Knueppel is a 3PM specialist with good FT% and points and no weak category. He fits any build that wants threes, but he gives little in steals and blocks. Every expert says his market rank in the 30s and 40s is too high and puts him in the 60s. ESPN has his average cost at 15.4 USD while Yahoo has it at 9.5 USD, and in an expert mock he sold for 13 USD against Josh's limit of 8 USD. So stay around 8 to 12 USD and let others pay more. Early in the season, check his hamstring after the week-one re-evaluation and whether his FG% holds near last season's 47.5% now that he takes more shots without LaMelo Ball.
